h1: The 6 Best Laptop Storage and Charging Carts of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Laptop Charging Carts 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six laptop storage and charging carts, from 16 to 36 device capacity, compared on locks, surge protection and assembly.
summary: The Meteteel 20-device cart is the best laptop charging cart, with independently locking front and back doors, a ventilated steel frame and 95 percent pre-assembly. The VEVOR holds 16 devices with a confirmed lock and surge protection, and the TIOPLY holds 36. The Plugsharge handles Chromebooks, the Pearington mixes tablets and laptops, and the Hupsjer is the budget cart.
intro: Buyers of charging carts usually count devices and stop. The costlier mistakes come afterward: a cart that arrives flat-packed and swallows a weekend, a cabinet with no real lock, or slots too narrow for the laptops you actually own. Heat and power are the quiet issues too, because twenty chargers running overnight in a closed box need ventilation and protection.

Our editors compared six carts by their spec pages and ranked them on the Primea score, giving the most weight to locking, capacity, power protection, screen limits and assembly. Prices are buckets only. We omitted the 18-device Meteteel because it shares a line with the 20-device cart, and we did not rank on weight or footprint, which most listings skip.

products.name: Meteteel Fully Assembled 20 Device Laptop Charging Cart for School (Black)
products.verdict: Twenty slots, locking front and back doors, and almost no assembly.
products.description:
The Meteteel 20-device cart has independently locking front and back doors, a ventilated steel frame and built-in cable management. It ships 95 percent pre-assembled and is priced $200 to $500. Ventilation matters because 20 chargers produce heat, and a closed box without airflow runs hot overnight.

It beats the VEVOR on capacity and locks both sides, and it saves hours on assembly that the flat-packed Pearington demands. Independent front and back locks let one person load while the other side stays secure.

Buy it for schools wanting a ready-to-roll cart. The caveats are the $200 to $500 price and that 20 slots may be more than a small team needs. Skip it if you only have a handful of devices.
cons: Sized for 20, may be too many
products.skipIf: You only have a handful of devices.

products.name: VEVOR 16 Device Charging Station with Lock & Key, Mobile Charging Cart
products.verdict: A confirmed lock and key, surge protection and 16 slots.
products.description:
The VEVOR holds 16 devices with a confirmed lock and key, built-in surge protection and an integrated power strip. It has two locking casters and is priced $200 to $500. Surge protection guards a row of chargers from a spike that could damage several devices at once.

It ranks just under the Meteteel because it holds four fewer devices and does not describe assembly, though the lock and surge protection are both confirmed. Against the TIOPLY, it is smaller but better documented on protection.

Buy it for medium-size classrooms and teams. The caveats are fewer slots than the leader and unstated assembly. Skip it if you need more than 16 slots.

products.name: TIOPLY 36 Device Charging Cart for Laptop Up to 16.3-inch Screen, Mobile Charging
products.verdict: The largest capacity here, 36 devices, with lock and key doors.
products.description:
The TIOPLY holds 36 devices and laptops up to 16.3 inches. It has lock and key doors, a power-line management bar and a mix of two fixed and two swivel wheels. It is priced $200 to $500. A 16.3 inch limit accommodates larger laptops that smaller carts reject.

It places third because its wheel setup lists no locking casters, which matters on a loaded cart, and it is large. It beats the Plugsharge on security because the doors lock.

Buy it for large fleets with big-screen laptops. The caveats are no locking casters and a likely large footprint. Skip it if your fleet is small.

products.name: Plugsharge 32-Device Laptop Charging Cart for Chromebooks, iPad & Tablets
products.verdict: Thirty-two numbered slots with individual cable organizers.
products.description:
The Plugsharge holds 32 devices up to 15.6 inches, with surge and ground fault protection, 32 individual cable organizers and numbered slots. Its open rack design is priced $200 to $500. Numbered slots with their own cable guides keep a Chromebook class in order, and ground fault protection adds safety.

It trails the TIOPLY because the open rack lists no door lock, so devices are visible and reachable. In a locked room that may be fine, but it is a security gap in a shared hallway.

Buy it for orderly Chromebook and tablet fleets. The caveats are no door lock and the $200 to $500 price. Skip it if you need locked storage.
cons: Open rack, no door lock listed

products.name: Pearington 30 Device Mobile Charging/Storage Cart for iPads, Tablets, Laptop
products.verdict: Thirty bays plus two bonus outlets, but you assemble it.
products.description:
The Pearington has 30 bays with 13 inch screen slots, cable management in the dividers and two bonus outlets, so 32 devices charge while 30 are stored and locked. It requires full assembly and is priced $200 to $500. Dividers that carry the cables keep the charging tidy.

It ranks below the Plugsharge because the 13 inch screen limit excludes bigger laptops and full assembly costs time. It does lock, which the Plugsharge does not.

Buy it for tablet-heavy fleets with some small laptops. The caveats are the assembly and the 13 inch limit. Skip it if you own larger laptops.
products.idealFor: Tablet-heavy fleets with some small laptops.

products.name: Hupsjer 16-Device Mobile Charging Cart, Laptop Charging Station w/Storage Shelf
products.verdict: A 16-device cart with a separate cable and adapter compartment, one tier cheaper.
products.description:
The Hupsjer holds 16 devices and adds a separate cable and adapter compartment measuring 25.2 by 15 by 3.5 inches. It has adjustable removable dividers, a padded shelf and 2 of 4 casters lock. It is priced $100 to $200. A separate compartment keeps adapters and cords from tangling in the slots.

It ran last because no lock or surge protection is stated and only half the casters brake. It costs a bucket less than the VEVOR, which does list both.

Buy it for small teams on a budget. The caveats are the missing lock and surge details. Skip it if security is the top priority.

methodology.title: Capacity
methodology.description: We compared how many devices each cart stores and charges.

methodology.title: Security
methodology.description: Locking doors or lock and key earned more credit than an open rack.

methodology.title: Power protection
methodology.description: Surge, ground fault and breaker details counted when listed.

methodology.title: Assembly
methodology.description: Pre-assembled carts beat flat-packs for the time they save.

methodology.title: Device size
methodology.description: Maximum screen size decides whether your laptops actually fit.

whatMatters.detail: This is how many laptops or tablets the cart stores and charges at once. It matters because buying too small forces a second cart. Count your devices and add room to grow, then read the capacity in the title, and remember that mixed devices may not all fit every slot. Tablets and thick laptops use slots differently.

A lock keeps devices in the cart overnight. Doors with lock and key protect better than an open rack. The listing states whether doors lock and how many, as with the Meteteel's independent front and back doors. Check this before ordering, since a cart without locks needs a locked room. Keys also need an owner.

Surge protection and breakers guard devices charging together. Without them, a power spike can damage several at once. Look for surge or breaker mentions in the specs, and note that the VEVOR and Plugsharge list protection while others leave it unstated. Cheap strips offer outlets but little protection.

Slots have a maximum screen size, such as 13, 14, 15.6 or 16.3 inches. Laptops that are bigger or thicker will not fit. Compare your laptop size to the listed limit, and measure thickness with a case on, since protective cases often make a laptop too wide. Allow a few millimeters for cables.

Some carts ship nearly assembled and some flat. A flat-pack can cost hours of time. The listing says pre-assembled, tool-free or full assembly required, so read it before you plan a weekend, since rolling a flat-pack from box to classroom adds a full day. The Meteteel is 95 percent assembled, while the Pearington needs full assembly.

faq.a: It is the same line as the 20-device cart, so we kept the larger one. Duplicating a product line adds no choice for the buyer, only noise.

faq.q: Do these protect against power surges?
faq.a: The VEVOR and Plugsharge list surge protection, and the others vary. Check the specs, and ask the seller about breakers when a listing says nothing. A protected power strip inside the cart is not the same as a surge-rated one.

The Plugsharge and TIOPLY list slots that size or larger, with the TIOPLY reaching 16.3 inches for bigger machines. Smaller carts such as the Pearington stop at 13 inches. Measure the thickest laptop in your fleet, with its case on.

faq.q: Is a locked cart worth it?
faq.a: For shared fleets, yes, because unattended laptops disappear. The Meteteel and VEVOR lock the doors, while the Plugsharge's open rack does not. A locked room can substitute, but it is a weaker arrangement.

The Meteteel is 95 percent pre-assembled, while the Pearington needs full assembly. That difference can save an afternoon. Ask whether tools are included, and plan two people for lifting a full-size cart.

faq.q: Can I roll a full cart?
faq.a: Yes, but only some casters lock, so brake it before loading or unloading. A loaded cart is heavy, and a rolling one is a hazard. The VEVOR has two locking casters and the Hupsjer two of four.

finalTake: Buy the Meteteel for a school that wants a ready-to-roll locked cart, and the VEVOR for a medium classroom. The TIOPLY is the large-fleet option, and the Plugsharge keeps Chromebooks orderly. Choose the Pearington for tablet-heavy fleets and the Hupsjer when budget outranks security. Confirm lock, surge protection and screen limit before ordering.
